analysis:
Reviewed the two supplied head_text units of desktop-app/package-lock.json (lines 1-1666). The PR is a lockfile-only dependency bump. Visible root changes: electron 44.5.1 -> 44.9.1 (line 24) and vite 8.3.2 -> 8.3.5 (line 31). Patch excerpts also show @oxc-project/types 0.152.0 -> 0.155.0 and @rolldown/binding-* 1.2.12 -> 1.2.15 (outside the supplied head lines, in later ranges). The supplied lines 1-1666 show no changed resolved URLs pointing at non-registry hosts, no git or tarball sources, and no removed integrity fields. Visible entries all use https://registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity hashes. The excerpt rows for the bumped packages carry new integrity values, as expected. I cannot verify those hashes against the registry. The bulk of the changed ranges (lines >1666, including the rolldown bindings, plus lines 5980-6010 region changes) were not in the supplied units, so they are unexamined here.

Threat-model relevance: this is the desktop-app build and dev toolchain, and it is not on the provider/coordinator WebSocket path (TB-002), the attestation chain (TB-009), App Attest authorization (TB-011), or the MLX inference engine (TB-007). No change to the A-001 to A-018 asset handling, key custody, attestation, routing gates or authorization is visible. Electron is the runtime of the desktop shell and signing and notarization tooling (@electron/osx-sign, electron-builder), so a toolchain supply-chain compromise would be relevant to T-013/T-034 artifact integrity in principle. However, the visible evidence shows only version bumps with registry integrity pins, which is not a regression. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the unseen changed lock ranges (rolldown bindings, lines 1869-2018 and 5998-6028 on the head side) keep registry resolved URLs and integrity hashes, and that electron 44.9.1 does not alter fuse or signing configuration (the electron-builder config is not in this batch).
